Responses in task data

Source: R/trials.R
gorilla_trials.Rd

Keeps the rows of the task data that hold a participant's response and gives them the same columns whether the task was made with Task Builder 1 or 2. Rows with instructions, continue buttons, fixation crosses, media events and other information are dropped.

Usage

gorilla_trials(x, task = NULL, all_rows = FALSE, quiet = FALSE)

Arguments

x

A gorilla_data object from read_gorilla().

task

Names of the tasks to include, as in the task_name column. All by default.

all_rows

Keep all rows of the trials, not only the responses. A column response_type then says what each row is, such as "response", "info" or a zone type.

quiet

If TRUE, no message about components without response values is shown.

Value

A tibble with one row per response and columns

participant_private_id, experiment_version, tree_node_key, repeat_key, task_name, task_version

Who did which task, in which version and node of the experiment, with Gorilla's Repeat Key.

spreadsheet

Name of the spreadsheet used.

trial

Trial number.

display, screen

Display and screen of the response. Task Builder 1 has no displays.

component, object

Component and object that recorded the response in Task Builder 2; zone type and zone name in Task Builder 1.

response

The response, as text.

rt

Reaction time in milliseconds.

correct

Whether the response was scored as correct.

time

Time of the response, in UTC.

followed by the timing columns of the export, such as reaction_onset in Task Builder 1 or onset_time, absolute_reaction_time and response_duration in Task Builder 2, and by the spreadsheet (spreadsheet_) and store (store_) columns. Only columns with values for the selected tasks are kept. All columns of the export remain in x$tasks.

Details

In Task Builder 2 a response is a row with response_type "response". In Task Builder 1 it is a row from a response zone (zone_type starting with response_).

Some components can record a response without a value, such as a Click Response whose objects have no response set up in 'Gorilla'. The clicked object is then only in object. When every response of a component in a task is empty, a message names the task and component. response is left empty, so use dplyr::coalesce(response, object) if the object names are the answers.

Examples

g <- read_gorilla(gorilla_example())
#> Skipped 1 file without data (nodes no participant reached): data_exp_123456-v3_questionnaire-zz1e.csv
gorilla_trials(g)
#> # A tibble: 127 × 23
#>    participant_private_id experiment_version tree_node_key repeat_key task_name 
#>    <chr>                               <int> <chr>         <chr>      <chr>     
#>  1 9100037                                 3 task-ld2k     NA         Lexical d…
#>  2 9100037                                 3 task-ld2k     NA         Lexical d…
#>  3 9100037                                 3 task-ld2k     NA         Lexical d…
#>  4 9100037                                 3 task-ld2k     NA         Lexical d…
#>  5 9100037                                 3 task-ld2k     NA         Lexical d…
#>  6 9100037                                 3 task-ld2k     NA         Lexical d…
#>  7 9100037                                 3 task-ld2k     NA         Lexical d…
#>  8 9100037                                 3 task-ld2k     NA         Lexical d…
#>  9 9100037                                 3 task-ld2k     NA         Lexical d…
#> 10 9100037                                 3 task-ld2k     NA         Lexical d…
#> # ℹ 117 more rows
#> # ℹ 18 more variables: task_version <int>, spreadsheet <chr>, trial <dbl>,
#> #   display <chr>, screen <chr>, component <chr>, object <chr>, response <chr>,
#> #   rt <dbl>, correct <lgl>, time <dttm>, spreadsheet_word <chr>,
#> #   spreadsheet_lexicality <chr>, spreadsheet_answer <chr>,
#> #   spreadsheet_row <int>, spreadsheet_word_1 <chr>, spreadsheet_word_2 <chr>,
#> #   spreadsheet_rhyme <chr>
gorilla_trials(g, task = "Lexical decision")
